title: TCS Launches Custom Chip Design Services for Automakers and Semiconductor Firms
excerpt: The end-to-end System-on-Chip design offering targets software-defined vehicles, extending TCS's push from IT services into semiconductor engineering.
body:
• Tata Consultancy Services on September 17 launched Custom System-on-Chip (SoC) Design Services for automotive original equipment manufacturers and semiconductor ecosystem players.
  • The end-to-end offering covers chip architecture, design, verification, implementation, software integration and system validation, aimed at software-defined vehicles.
  • TCS says the move responds to automakers' demand for customised computing as vehicles shift toward centralised computing, ADAS and electrification.
  • The launch deepens India's push into semiconductor design at a time when the country's chip market is projected to double to over $100 billion by 2030.

Tata Consultancy Services on Thursday launched Custom System-on-Chip (SoC) Design Services for automotive original equipment manufacturers and semiconductor ecosystem players, marking the IT services giant's most direct move yet into the business of designing the silicon that powers modern vehicles.

The end-to-end semiconductor engineering service is designed to help automakers conceive, design, verify, implement and validate custom SoC solutions for the next generation of software-defined vehicles (SDVs), the company said in a statement reported by The Hindu BusinessLine.

Why automakers want their own chips

The automotive industry is undergoing a structural shift. Vehicle architectures are moving toward centralised computing and zonal networks, while advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS), electric powertrains and connected features demand computing built for specialised workloads. As software takes on a larger role in what a vehicle does, automakers are seeking greater control over the silicon beneath their platforms.

Custom SoCs allow automakers to align compute capabilities with their software requirements, improve performance-per-watt and differentiate user experiences — the same logic that pushed Tesla, Volkswagen and several Chinese automakers to bring chip design in-house over the past decade.

"Silicon is becoming a strategic enabler of innovation, influencing everything from vehicle performance and energy efficiency to software capabilities and user experience."

— Sreenivasa Chakravarti, Global Head and Vice President, Industrial Autonomy and Engineering, TCS

"The concept of AI-SDV-driven mobility will be differentiated by the computing architecture on which it runs," Chakravarti said in the company's announcement. "TCS brings together semiconductor engineering, embedded software, and systems expertise to help automakers translate their silicon strategies into differentiated mobility platforms."

What the service covers

TCS said the offering brings together semiconductor engineering, VLSI (Very Large-Scale Integration) design, hardware-software co-design and system validation. The comprehensive set of services covers every stage of silicon development: architecture, design, verification, implementation, software integration and system validation.

According to TechCircle, TCS will apply a chip-to-system engineering approach — considering vehicle architecture, software platforms, workloads and compute requirements before defining the SoC architecture — rather than treating silicon as a standalone engineering programme. The intent is to connect chip development with the wider vehicle development lifecycle.

India's semiconductor moment

The launch lands in the middle of India's accelerating semiconductor push. The Union Cabinet has approved the India Semiconductor Mission with a ₹76,000 crore outlay covering fabrication, design and manufacturing, and the country's chip market is projected to more than double from an estimated $45-50 billion in 2024-25 to $100-110 billion by 2030, according to Outlook Business.

India is already home to roughly 20 percent of the world's chip design engineers, and global players are investing in manufacturing and assembly facilities. TCS is no stranger to the sector — the company recently launched chiplet-based system engineering services for semiconductor firms, including advanced package design such as 2.5D and 3D interposers aimed at accelerating chiplet tape-out.

The new automotive SoC offering extends that trajectory: TCS is positioning itself not just as a services vendor to chipmakers, but as an engineering partner to car companies that are themselves becoming technology companies.

What to watch

Whether the offering wins traction will depend on automaker appetite for outsourcing silicon strategy to an IT services firm rather than building it internally or working with established chip designers. The first customer wins — and the terms TCS strikes on intellectual property and design reuse — will say a great deal about how far a services-led model can go in the chip business.

For India's semiconductor ambitions, though, the signal is clear: the country's largest IT services firm now treats chip design as a growth engine, and the talent pipeline that makes that possible — India's deep bench of VLSI and embedded engineers — is increasingly the country's competitive advantage in the race for the software-defined vehicle.
nri_angle: For NRIs following India's tech ascent, TCS's move into custom chip design for global automakers is a marker of how far Indian engineering services have climbed the value chain — from back-office IT to the silicon inside next-generation vehicles.
